title: Longest Common Prefix After at Most One Removal
summary: Given two strings s and t , find the length of the longest common prefix between them after removing at most one character from s .
statement: Given two strings s and t , find the length of the longest common prefix between them after removing at most one character from s . Note that s can remain unchanged if no character is removed.
constraints: s and t are nonempty lowercase strings.
Remove at most one character from s only; leaving s unchanged is allowed.
Return the maximum common-prefix length between the resulting s and t.
hints: Before the first mismatch, skipping that source character is the only removal that can extend the prefix.
Scan both strings; on the first mismatch advance only s, then require exact matches thereafter.
Advance both pointers on equality, consume the one removal on mismatch, and stop at a second mismatch.
Removing earlier equal characters would immediately shorten the prefix, while removing later cannot repair the first mismatch.
editorial: Removing earlier equal characters would immediately shorten the prefix, while removing later cannot repair the first mismatch.

tests.explanation: After matching mad, remove x from s and match a, producing prefix length four.
Removing the initial x lets all four target characters match.
